transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
The pilot, who was attacked in the cockpit during a flight, is speaking out days after
what authorities have called an attempted terrorist attack.
Captain Smit Machar spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday.
He said his co-pilot asked to pray before striking him from behind during Wednesday's
flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
My first thought was that there was a catastrophic damage to the aircraft, and something is not
right.
But then after that, the blue book kept coming, one after the other.
And that's when I realized that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the
cockpit with me.
Investigators say the co-pilot attacked him with a crash axe and tried to seize control
of the plane.
Officials say a passenger helped steady the aircraft before a third pilot took over and
landed safely in Saudi Arabia.
A planned release of emergency oil reserves could help ease pressure on global diesel markets.
NPR's Julia Simon reports G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of
oil and refine products over the next four months.
In recent weeks, diesel prices have reached record highs, pushed up by shortages and damage
to refineries in the Middle East and Russia, as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to hit
Russian refineries.
Last month, diesel topped $6.50 a gallon here in the U.S.
For context, diesel was around $3.75 in September of last year.
That's more than 70 percent lower.
Diesel prices are even higher in some European countries.
Earlier, President Trump had threatened to cut off U.S. diesel exports, which both American
oil companies and European leaders opposed.
Julia Simon, NPR News.
Wall Street is heading into a light week in terms of economic data with investors mainly
focused on bonds.
NPR's Raphael Nam reports those markets continue to signal big concerns about the global economy.
It's been a volatile stretch in the bond markets, which have tumbled recently over worries
about inflation.
Stock investors tend to focus on company profits.
But bond investors tend to be pretty sensitive to economic trends.
And right now, there is room for concern.
Tensions with Iran continue, keeping energy costs high at a time when inflation is already
pretty elevated.
The Federal Reserve has responded by raising interest rates last month.
But policymakers want to be cautious, given all the uncertainty about the economy.
The result is that bond investors are nervous.
And those nerves are now spreading to stock markets as well.
Raphael Nam, NPR News.
This is NPR.
The Supreme Court opens its new term tomorrow with a case that could shape whether communities
can sue oil and gas companies over climate change.
Officials in Boulder County, Colorado, want the companies to help pay for damage from
disasters linked to a warming climate.
It's one of dozens of governments across the country bringing similar lawsuits with billions
of dollars at stake.
The energy companies argue that climate change is a global issue that should not be decided
in state courts.
The justices will decide on the case at the end of its term next June.
The Milwaukee Brewers beat the San Diego Padres last night in the Major League Baseball playoffs.
Chuck Kornbach reports a key play involved a fly ball that hit a roof cable before being
caught for an out.
Padres first baseman Ty France had a very high fly in the ninth inning that may have
gone for a go-ahead two-run home run, but the baseball glanced off a cable supporting
the retractable roof at American Family Field, and Brewers left fielder Jackson Churio caught
the ball for an out.
After Milwaukee won the game 3-2, manager Pat Murphy credited the spirit of late Brewers
announcer Bob Yooker.
Yook decided to put his hand on it and swat it down so Churio could catch it.
So thanks, Yook.
The win gives the Brewers a one-game-to-nothing lead over the Padres in their best-of-five
National League division series.
For NPR News, I'm Chuck Kornbach in Milwaukee.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: Co-pilot attacked captain with crash axe during flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday
G7 leaders agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and refined products over four months
Bond market volatility signals investor concerns about global economy and inflation
Supreme Court opens term with case on whether communities can sue oil companies over climate damage
Milwaukee Brewers beat San Diego Padres in MLB playoffs after fly ball hits roof cable
